name: 1919 Prairie Avenue — Marshall Field Jr. house, after its 1902 enlargement, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet labels the building with a 1911 use, '2½S.B. brick The Gatlin Institute', which the draft does not carry back to 1904 (the T-1837 register warns not to assume the 1904 use from it). The register's family row, 'Field Jr., post-1902 enlargement', names it a house, so the 1904 function is inferred residence on that row and the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'Marshall Field Jr. Residence. Built 1867', enlarged several times, the last in 1902.

research_note: T-3279 (piece 1 of T-1906) refines the district draft (T-2330) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt on the K01 frontage assembly and its kits instead of the draft builder, from the two Gatlin Institute advertisement plates (the 1912 Chicago Blue Book's and the 1913 Daily News Almanac's, both photographs of c. 1909-1912, public domain) against the 1911 Sanborn sheet 28. The plates show the house as Marshall Field Jr.'s 1902 enlargement left it (the Institute bought it in 1909 and changed its use, not its form): a narrow red brick front with a canted north corner and a stoop at its south end, a long north flank with a round tower close behind the front, two very tall stacks, steep slated roofs with dormers and gables. The 1913 plate's camera is solved and its match record written (differs); the other pictures (the c. 1905 Daily News negative, the before-1902 photograph of the earlier front, the 1919 programme, the 1981 and 2004 photographs, the elevations drawing) are T-3280's. Liberty L-k01-1919-field-jr-3279 records what is built without a reading.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws it and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped); the 1912 and 1913 plates photograph it c. 1909-1912 in the form its 1902 enlargement gave it. Its building and loss dates are T-1907's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1919 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1919 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).
position.note: The rear north corner of the main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (T-3279): the draft frame's u 6.80, v -0.80 (lot frame u 28.300, v -1.550 from the middle of the rear lot line), where the traced front block's rear (the step to the wider middle range) meets its north wall. Through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation 179.445 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, so v runs SOUTH: K01's 'south' wall is the real north flank.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is read from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel with tools/draft_prairie_1904.py's lot_frame and to_uv (T-3279).

footprint.note: The front block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1919-b1, data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s28.json): in the draft's frame its rear at u 6.8 (where the plan steps out to the middle range), its front wall at 25.2 (18.4 m deep), its north wall at v -0.8 and its south wall at 9.1 (9.9 m along the street). The sheet draws the front swelling forward to u 26.0 between corners cut back to 25.2 (v 0.4-8.8): that swell is the bowed front of the 1913 plate, built as a K08 bow (bays). The north wall's shallow bows (about 0.6 m, u 9.4-19.3) are the tower's and the stack's. What stands behind the block is the rear wings'.

stories.note: '2½S.B.' printed on the 1911 sheet over the front block, and both Gatlin plates show it: two full storeys of brick over a raised basement and a half storey in the roof, lit by dormers.

construction.note: The sheet colours the house pink (brick) and prints 'S.B.' (stone basement); the 1912, 1913 and 1919 plates show red pressed brick walls over a pale stone basement, dressed in pale stone string courses at the floors and bands at the sills and heads. T-3305: built as K01's brick front over a K02 stone basement (stone_front.brick_above_m), which lays the stone belts at the floor lines and the bands at the window lines across the brick, with the basement's stone carried round both flanks (side_base).

stone_front.note: T-3305: the sheet's 'S.B.' and all three plates' pale basement under the brick, and the plates' pale courses across the brick at each floor and window line (the programme plate draws them plainest on the rear ranges' bays, whose stone is T-3303's). Built as K02's smooth Lemont limestone to the principal floor (brick_above_m 1.7, the record's principal_floor_m), and the plates' three pale courses across the brick named (stone_front.belts): one under the principal sills (2.30-2.45 m), the belt at the second floor (5.60-5.80 m) and one under the chamber sills (6.25-6.40 m). INFERRED: the stone's kind and dressing are not readable in the halftones; its pale tone and the courses' places are the plates', their depths the kit's.

side_base.note: T-3305: the programme plate shows the pale basement carried round the north flank (K01's south wall) under its brick; the south wall (K01's north), about 1 m off 1923's, is taken to match it (the sheet's 'S.B.' is the whole house's).

side_belts.note: T-3305: the plates show pale stone courses across the front block's brick and the programme plate draws them along the north flank's rear ranges; the main block's own flank (K01's south wall) stands mostly behind the lamp and the ivy in the programme plate, so its courses are the front's three carried round at the same lines, in place of K03's brick string course. INFERRED: that the courses run round is the plates'; the lines on this wall are the front's, the 0.15-0.2 m depths and 0.05 m projection the kit's.

principal_floor_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a high stoop at the front's south end, which both plates show climbing to the door; its height is not readable in the halftones, so the principal floor is taken at 1.7 m (ten risers, which the K07 stoop and the K01 stair solve alike) inside the contract's range.

storey_heights_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two tall storeys of a large house, the principal one the taller; the wall head stands at 9.5 m, which the 1913 plate's camera puts at the eave line it shows over the front (data/reference_views/marshall_field_jr_house_1919_prairie/cdn_almanac_1913.json).

wall_thickness_side_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the sheet prints '12' (inches) against the walls; K01 lays it at 0.33 with its joints.

service_wall_brick.note: Every wall the plates show, the street front and the long north flank alike, is the same dark red brick, so the K03 red-brown panel is laid all round rather than the buff common brick; the 2004 photograph of the restored house shows red brick on both faces.

street_front_trim.note: RECONSTRUCTED: stone lintels over every window: the plates show square-headed windows in the brick under pale heads, too small in the halftone to read a profile.

wall_head.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K10's bracketed eave cornice under the hip, the kit's cornice for a hip; the plates show a heavy eave carried round the front and its canted corner, its profile not readable.

roof_form.note: The plates show the front block under a steep slated roof with a dormer on its street slope, and no flat deck or mansard curb; built as K01's hip, its ridge running front to back. The plates' gables on the north flank are the rear ranges' (rear_wings).

roof_pitch_deg.note: T-3280: read off the 1919 programme plate through its solved camera (data/reference_views/marshall_field_jr_house_1919_prairie/gatlin_programme_1919.json): the street hip's apex, where its finial stands, lies at about 15.9 m over grade, so 6.4 m over the 9.5 m eave across the front block's 4.95 m half-depth, about 52 degrees. The 1913 plate shows the roof as steep. T-3279 had built it at 45, the top of K01's ordinary band, until a reading could be measured.

eave_overhang_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K05 eave over the bracketed cornice, 1712's.

roof_covering.note: The plates show a dark, small-unit covering on every slope, read as slate; copper flashings and ridge roll are the kit's.

dormer.note: The broad gabled dormer on the street slope over the front, which the 1919 programme plate shows with three lights under its gable, as the 1913 plate does: T-3280 built it 3.3 m wide with three K06 sashes at the contract's narrowest, 0.75 m, 1.0 m apart (K01's `sash.at_m`), still centred on the front. Where it stands along the front the pictures do not agree: through the programme plate's camera its face lies about 1.6 m south of the centre, while the 2004 photograph (unsolved) shows it about 1 m north of it, so it stays on the centre, between them, and the difference is within tolerance. T-3301 adds what both Gatlin plates draw beside and over it. The smaller one-light dormer near the front's south end (`also`): the programme plate's source record names it, and the 2004 photograph (unsolved; read at about 57 px to the metre across the 9.9 m front) puts its centre about 8.0 m from the north corner and its face about 1.6 m wide with one tall light; built at v 8.05 m, 1.6 m wide, one K06 sash of the broad dormer's size, its face, setback, pitch and verges the broad one's (K01's `dormer.also`). Its width and its light are INFERRED from the 2004 photograph, its existence and place from the plates. And the stone-coped gable (`coping`): both plates draw the broad dormer's gable pale against the slate, carried up over the roof with kneelers at its feet and a finial at its apex, and the 2004 photograph shows both dormers' gables coped in stone with kneelers. Built as an 0.18 m stone coping along each rake, 0.35 m back from the face, 0.35 m kneelers and a 0.45 m turned finial on the broad dormer's apex (the small dormer takes the same build): the coping's depth, the kneelers' size and the finial's height and turning are RECONSTRUCTED at the plates' scale, which does not resolve them (L-k01-1919-coped-dormers-3301).

entrance_bay.note: The door at the front's south end (K01's 'north' in this frame), where both plates show the stoop climbing beside the south neighbour.

front_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED in its windows: the front wall's own column is the door's at the south end, with a window over it, where the plates show the stoop and an arched opening beside the south neighbour; the rest of the front is the bow (bays), whose windows are the front's. The plates show the front too obliquely and under trees to count its windows.

side_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a window a storey along the main body's north flank (K01's south wall) behind the tower: the 1913 plate shows windows in two storeys there, but not where along the wall.

north_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two windows a storey in the south wall (K01's north), which stands about 1 m off the lot line facing 1923's north wall.

rear_bays.note: None: the middle range (rear_wings) covers the whole rear wall on the 1911 sheet.

sash_by_storey.note: RECONSTRUCTED: tall two-storey sash, the principal storey's the taller; the plates show tall square-headed windows. T-3280: the upper storey's lights 1.8 m high, 0.15 m under T-3279's, so their lintels clear the soffit and the cornice's bed of the 52-degree hip, whose overhang drops further down its slope.

basement_lights.note: RECONSTRUCTED: lights in the stone basement ('S.B.') under the principal windows.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K06 two-over-two double-hung sash (the kit has no flat-headed one-over-one; the plates cannot resolve the glazing bars); the basement lights the kit's area light.

chimneys.note: The two tall stacks the 1913 plate shows rising off the north flank well above the ridge: one between the round tower and the front's canted corner, one further back. Their places along the wall are read through the plate's camera; their plans and their height, 1.6 m over the ridge (K01 tops a hip's stacks off the ridge), is RECONSTRUCTED at about what the plates show: T-3280 steepened the hip to 52 degrees, lifting the ridge 1.4 m, and lowered the stacks' rise by as much, so their tops stand where T-3279 put them, about 17.4 m, which the 1913 plate's camera reads at 17.1 m and 17.7 m and the 1919 programme plate's at 16.8 m and 18.1 m (the near stack and the far one). T-3301 adds the third, the stack both Gatlin plates draw rising behind the street dormers at the front block's south side (the programme plate's source record: 'a stack behind them'), which the 2004 photograph shows between the broad dormer and the small one, close behind them: built at u 14.5 m, v 7.5 m, just behind the small dormer's body and clear of the broad one's, where the programme plate's camera stands it at the broad dormer's south cheek, on the kit's 0.9 x 0.75 m plan and the stacks' shared 1.6 m over the ridge. Its place is INFERRED from the pictures (none of them is solved for it), its plan and height RECONSTRUCTED as the others'.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: half-round copper gutters on the hip's eaves and round downpipes at the north flank's rear end and the south wall's front end; the street front, whose corner brackets the kit stands at both ends, carries none.

entrance_kit.note: T-3305: the 1912 and 1913 plates show a round-arched opening at the stoop's head beside the south neighbour; built as K07's round-arched entrance, its pair of leaves set in the arch's reveal under a fanlight, at the head of the straight stoop; the front wall stands 7.98 m from the 1904 parcel's street line (the sheet's bow comes 0.8 m nearer, its 7.15 m). INFERRED: the arch is the plates'; its opening (1.3 by 3.3 m), its stone ring and keystone (the arch's dressing, as 1834's), the 0.4 m reveal in the 0.45 m wall, the leaves and the fanlight are the kit's, the halftones too coarse to read them.

bays.note: (1) FRONT_BOW: the broad bow across the front's north part, which the 1913 plate shows as the curved eave and wall sweeping from the north corner along the front, and which the 1911 sheet draws as the front swelling 0.8 m forward of corners cut back at v 0.4 and 8.8 (in this frame). Built as a K08 bow, 6.0 m on its chord and 1.0 m out (K08's facet and window rules refuse a flatter one), two storeys of three windows, its nearly flat tin cap tucked under the main cornice's bed (K08 stops a bay below it), where the plate carries the eave itself round the bow; its windows and their heights are RECONSTRUCTED. (2) NORTH_TOWER: the round tower on the north flank close behind the front, which the 1913 plate shows rising through both storeys and a stage past the eave with tall windows round it, and which stands there still (the 2004 photograph). Its place along the wall, s 13.4 m from the rear corner, is the plate's through its camera; the 1911 sheet bows the north wall out about 0.6-1.0 m there. It is built half-engaged, 2.6 m across with its centre 0.1 m before the wall plane, so it stands 1.4 m out where the sheet's bow reads 0.6-1.0 m. Its radius, storey heights, windows and low slated cap are RECONSTRUCTED: the halftone cannot resolve the top. T-3280: (2) NORTH_TOWER's top: the 1919 programme plate and the 1913 plate both show the tower carried up past its third tier of windows as a plain band to a flat top with a heavy edge, its top at about 13.7 m and 14.9 m through their cameras, where T-3279's slated cone rose from 12.1 m to a finial at 14.4 m; built by carrying its third storey up 1.9 m, plain over its windows, to 14.0 m under K08's nearly flat tin cap (its eaves the heavy edge), and the cone and finial taken off. (3) FRONT_BOW's upper storey 2.4 m and its lights 1.7 m, 0.2 and 0.1 m under T-3279's, so the bow still stops under the cornice's bed, which the steeper hip's soffit brings 0.1 m lower. T-3305: the bow and the tower stand on the house's stone basement (plinth_m 1.7, the basement's top), the plates' pale base carried round both under their brick.

rear_wings.note: The ranges the 1911 sheet draws behind the front block, read off its trace (s28fp-1919-b1) in this frame (v runs south, K01's 'south' wall is the real north flank): (1) MIDDLE_RANGE, u -7.0 to 0, v -3.1 to 10.85, '2½S.B.', stepping out 3.1 m north of the front block and to the south lot line; (2) REAR_RANGE, u -16.4 to -7.0, v -4.8 to 10.8, '2½S.B.', a further 1.7 m north (its canted north bay, about 1.4 m out from u -14.5 to -9.4 on the sheet, is not yet built); (3) GARAGE, u -28.2 to -16.4, the sheet's '2B' 'GARAGE CEMENT FL'R' to the alley, its floor near grade. The two half-storey ranges are built under slated gables facing north and south, the steep gables the 1913 plate shows along the north flank; their pitch, heights and windows are RECONSTRUCTED. Whether the garage stood by 1904 the sheet cannot say (it is 1911's); it is carried as part of the building the T-1841 census rules present_as_mapped.

boundary.note: The iron fence on the street line that both plates show along the front and the north yard, with a gate at the walk; its pattern is not readable in the halftones and is K11's scroll band, as 1905's next door. A second gate on piers closes the side passage into the north yard (RECONSTRUCTED: K11 gates an iron front's side passage; its place is the kit's).

yard.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the walk in flags from the stair's foot through the fence's gate to the public walk, the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year; liberty L-k01-1919-field-jr-3279.
